findings.surface: Login, shell, and all owner routes
prerequisites: Site has ADMIN_API_KEY and normal site-to-API connectivity
reproduction: Set Cookie: myst-admin-session=definitely-not-the-admin-key.
Request /team?tab=access or an owner /api/team/access route.
Observe that source logic treats cookie presence as owner and callAdminApi adds the genuine server key and owner actor role.
findings.expected: A fabricated legacy cookie is rejected before page rendering or upstream access.
findings.actual: Any nonempty legacy admin cookie is accepted as owner; the equivalent crew cookie is accepted as crew.
findings.impact: Authentication bypass can expose PII and permit owner-only financial, access, messaging, automation, export, and destructive actions.
findings.likelyCause: Duplicated break-glass cookie presence checks instead of a centralized verified principal.
findings.recommendation: Centralize session verification, validate or remove legacy cookies, and reject before any server-side privileged helper runs.
acceptanceCriteria: Arbitrary and empty admin/crew cookie values redirect to /team/login and return 401 from JSON routes.
Only a cryptographically verified, unexpired, active principal reaches owner or crew content.
The upstream API is not called when verification fails.
Regression tests cover page loads, exports, uploads, proxy routes, and representative mutations.

findings.surface: Same-origin /api/team proxies, server actions, and auxiliary instant-quote page
findings.subview: Media analysis, agent memory/next action, quote photos, Inbox suggestion, instant-quote detail/list
findings.dataState: known contact/thread UUID for resource-specific proxies; any path segment for the instant-quote page/list
prerequisites: Site ADMIN_API_KEY and Site-to-API connectivity
Known resource UUID only for resource-specific probes
AI/provider configuration only for cost-generating probes
reproduction: Without cookies, call /api/team/contacts/media-analysis?contactId=<known-id>.
Repeat against sales-agent-memory, sales-agent-next-action, quote-photos, and Inbox suggestion routes.
Without cookies, request /team/instant-quotes/not-a-real-id; the page has no auth layout/guard and still renders a privileged latest-25 list request.
Use a Delete form from that latest-25 list; no authenticated principal is checked before deleteInstantQuoteAction calls the key-only DELETE endpoint.
Observe that handlers parse parameters and call callAdminApi without requireTeamRole.
Observe that key-only upstreams accept the injected server key; permission-gated upstreams return full access when actor role and ID are both absent.
findings.expected: Every human-facing proxy and server action authenticates and authorizes before input parsing or upstream access; missing identity fails closed.
findings.actual: Multiple public proxies and the auxiliary page call callAdminApi without user authentication. Key-only upstreams accept the injected server key unconditionally; permission-gated upstreams additionally fail open when both actor role and actor ID are absent (an environment-provided default actor can alter that second path).
findings.impact: The source establishes unauthenticated PII/quote-analytics disclosure and an unauthenticated instant-quote deletion path; the sibling route also inherits the root's index/follow default because /team has no shared noindex layout. Other exposed proxies can trigger AI cost or draft, automation, and task mutations; outbound messaging through separately unguarded action references remains runtime-conditional.
findings.likelyCause: The internal admin credential is reused as end-user authorization and the permission layer deliberately fails open for missing actor headers.
findings.recommendation: Require one verified user/service principal everywhere, fail closed, and enforce permissions on the upstream endpoint as defense in depth.
acceptanceCriteria: All /api/team routes return 401 before parameter validation for anonymous requests.
Anonymous instant-quote detail/list requests redirect or return 401 before any customer or aggregate fetch.
Anonymous users cannot render or invoke instant-quote delete forms, and the upstream DELETE independently requires an authorized human principal.
A shared authenticated-product layout applies noindex/nofollow to every /team route, including auxiliary detail pages.
Authenticated denied users receive 403 and no upstream request occurs.
Human requests with no actor role/ID fail closed; workers use explicit service principals.
Direct server-action tests reject anonymous and underprivileged callers.
Contacts, properties, pipeline, and CRM task APIs enforce explicit read/write permissions.

prerequisites: Active session for a non-owner/non-office/non-crew role
reproduction: Create a valid sales, read_only, or custom role and session.
Load /team: page authentication accepts only owner, office, or crew and redirects.
POST directly to /api/team/contacts with that valid low-privilege session: resolveTeamRoleFromRequest coerces the role to office for the proxy's local gate.
Observe that callAdminApi forwards the original member/role, but the upstream contact create endpoint checks only the shared key and performs no granular permission check.
findings.expected: The exact role and effective grants/denies govern navigation, direct URLs, reads, mutations, exports, and current sessions.
findings.actual: Supported roles are locked out of the page yet coerced to office for site-proxy role gates. The original principal reaches upstream, but key-only core APIs still accept unauthorized reads and mutations.
findings.impact: Least privilege is unreliable: legitimate staff are blocked while low-privilege users may reach office-level contact reads or mutations through proxies.
findings.likelyCause: Three separate authorization models—role slug gates, effective permissions, and internal-key API gates—drift independently.
findings.recommendation: Make effective permissions the sole source of truth and preserve exact role/principal data through every hop.
acceptanceCriteria: Owner, office, sales, crew, read-only, and custom roles can authenticate without coercion.
Deny wins immediately in navigation, direct URLs, reads, mutations, exports, and existing sessions.
No role slug is implicitly promoted to office.
A generated role × permission × tab × action integration matrix passes.

findings.role: valid team owner or team office
prerequisites: Valid team session without a legacy admin/crew cookie
reproduction: Sign in as a team owner and open Commissions.
Submit payout-run or settings forms.
Observe that the proxy checks only myst-admin-session and rejects the valid team session.
As a valid team user, create a contact note and then attempt edit/delete; those handlers also check only legacy cookies.
findings.expected: A valid team principal can complete every action allowed by effective permissions without a second legacy login.
findings.actual: The UI renders, then selected mutations return unauthorized or Owner login required.
findings.impact: Critical financial and CRM maintenance workflows are blocked for the supported login path.
findings.likelyCause: Migration from break-glass cookies to team sessions is incomplete.
findings.recommendation: Route every mutation through the centralized principal/permission helper and remove route-local cookie checks.
acceptanceCriteria: A team owner can create, adjust, lock, pay, and reimburse a payout run without a legacy cookie; report/export routes retain their existing team-owner support.
Allowed team users can edit/delete notes and denied users receive 403.
All actions record the team member actor, not team-console.

findings.subview: Quotes, Policy, Automation, Marketing, SEO, Sales Log, Audit
prerequisites: Role default permissions
reproduction: As office, navigate to Policy, Automation, or Audit: permissions allow the tab but render branches require owner.
As crew, open Quotes: nav requires appointments.read and render allows crew, while quote APIs require quote permissions the default crew lacks.
findings.expected: One permission map controls visibility, rendering, and the API action set.
findings.actual: Navigation can expose blank or nonfunctional surfaces because nav requirements, role render gates, and API permissions disagree.
findings.impact: Users encounter blank pages or visible workflows that fail after effort; support cannot reason reliably about access.
findings.likelyCause: Permission metadata is duplicated in tab declarations, JSX role checks, and API routes.
findings.recommendation: Generate nav and render policy from the same permission contract used by the API.
acceptanceCriteria: Every visible tab renders a meaningful allowed state for the current principal.
Direct URL behavior matches navigation visibility.
Crew quote visibility and available actions match effective quote permissions.
Denied tabs render a deliberate 403/redirect state, never an empty main region.

prerequisites: Upstream returns non-2xx without throwing
reproduction: Force appointment status, appointment note, or quote decision upstream response to 403/409/500.
Submit the action.
Observe that the response is not checked and a success flash is written.
findings.expected: Non-success responses preserve input/state and show an actionable error; the UI never claims success.
findings.actual: Selected actions unconditionally display Appointment updated, Note added, or Quote updated after any returned response.
findings.impact: Staff can act on false state, miss failed notes or decisions, and create customer/revenue discrepancies.
findings.likelyCause: Early server actions predate the shared error-response pattern used by newer actions.
findings.recommendation: Require checked response helpers, preserve form state, and make retries idempotent.
acceptanceCriteria: All mutations branch on response.ok and map 401/403/409/422/429/500/timeout distinctly.
No success flash appears when the database mutation did not commit.
Duplicate click and retry tests prove idempotency or safe conflict handling.

findings.surface: Orphaned auxiliary Instant Quote Detail (not mounted or linked from canonical /team)
findings.role: intended staff user (route is anonymous under TEAM-AUTHZ-002)
prerequisites: A valid instant quote
reproduction: Open /team/instant-quotes/<id>.
Activate Book from this quote.
Observe that the link targets the same detail URL with prefill query parameters.
Observe that the page component accepts only params.id and never consumes searchParams.
findings.expected: The CTA enters a real booking flow with quote/contact/property data prefilled exactly once.
findings.actual: The CTA reloads the same detail/list page and ignores the prefill parameters.
findings.impact: Users who reach the auxiliary surface cannot convert from its primary CTA. No canonical /team ingress is present, so primary-workflow reach is unproven without telemetry or staff evidence.
findings.likelyCause: The handoff route was never connected after the auxiliary detail page was introduced.
findings.recommendation: Handoff to the canonical booking workflow and consolidate instant quotes into Quotes.
acceptanceCriteria: The CTA opens the canonical booking UI, not the same detail route.
Contact, property, scope, price, source quote, and attribution are prefilled and reviewable.
Successful booking links the appointment and quote and is idempotent on refresh.

findings.dataState: record with linked appointments, quotes, tasks, messages, payments, or partner data
prerequisites: A linked record
reproduction: Enter raw primary and duplicate contact UUIDs in Manual merge and submit; the form offers no identity/impact preview or confirmation.
Select a merge suggestion and activate Approve merge; no impact preview or confirmation is presented.
Approve and decline the same pending suggestion concurrently; both paths perform an unlocked read/status check and later updates do not predicate on status=pending.
Merge a source with AI-memory/next-action or partner user/rate/booking rows; mergeContacts moves only selected core rows and source deletion cascades the rest.
Delete a contact whose normalized phone is shared by another quote customer; the endpoint deletes every instant quote matching those digits.
Observe that the UI does not enumerate affected linked entities or a recovery path.
findings.expected: Destructive operations show exact affected entities, require explicit confirmation, enforce concurrency, audit the transaction, and document recovery.
findings.actual: Merge approval is one click; concurrent decisions are not compare-and-set; source-only AI/partner state cascades away; the merge suggestion itself cascades away instead of remaining a ledger; and contact deletion removes instant quotes by shared normalized phone rather than contact identity.
findings.impact: A mistaken or racing click can silently lose source-only AI/partner state, produce conflicting reviewer outcomes, delete another customer's same-phone quote, or unlink/remove operational and financial context.
findings.likelyCause: Database cascade behavior and UI confirmation patterns evolved independently.
findings.recommendation: Add server-generated previews, explicit typed confirmation for high-impact cases, optimistic concurrency, and a reversible merge ledger/backup process.
acceptanceCriteria: Preview counts and identifies properties, threads, tasks, appointments, quotes, payments, partners, and automation state.
Contact deletion targets instant quotes by an explicit relationship, never merely a shared normalized phone.
Stale or duplicate requests return 409 and make no changes.
Post-transaction links and audit evidence identify source, target, actor, and consolidation rules.
A tested recovery procedure exists.

findings.dataState: same-address contacts or partial address edit
prerequisites: Two contacts at one address or a partial property patch
reproduction: Add the same street/postal/state property to two different contacts; the global unique index rejects it.
Observe contact creation maps a property uniqueness conflict to contact_already_exists.
Patch only city/state/postal or one address field; geocoding is called with omitted fields replaced by empty/undefined and may clear coordinates.
findings.expected: Shared addresses are modeled intentionally, conflicts name the real entity, and partial edits geocode the complete merged address without losing valid coordinates on provider failure.
findings.actual: Address uniqueness is global, errors are mislabeled, and partial patches can geocode incomplete data then null coordinates.
findings.impact: Households/property managers cannot be represented reliably and valid geolocation may be silently lost.
findings.likelyCause: Address deduplication was implemented as ownership uniqueness and patch logic does not merge persisted fields before geocoding.
findings.recommendation: Separate property identity from contact association or scope uniqueness correctly; geocode a full merged address transactionally.
acceptanceCriteria: Documented same-address scenarios can be stored without duplicate property corruption.
409 responses identify the conflicting property/contact accurately.
Partial edits preserve untouched address fields and coordinates when geocoding fails.
Dependent appointment/quote links remain intact after edits.

findings.subview: Unmounted upload action and attachment link renderer
findings.role: intended /team editor; no active canonical /team submitter
findings.dataState: malicious URL, MIME mismatch, or large data URL
prerequisites: Legacy EstimatesSection or its attachment action is intentionally remounted
reproduction: Inspect EstimatesSection and addApptAttachmentAction: the legacy form converts a File to a base64 data URL and renders stored URLs as links.
Inspect the shared API boundary: it accepts an arbitrary nonempty URL/claimed contentType and can store up to 20 MB inline.
Confirm canonical /team Calendar neither mounts EstimatesSection nor offers this attachment form/link renderer.
findings.expected: Dormant upload code is removed, or it is security-reviewed and hardened before any /team remount.
findings.actual: The only /team submitter/renderer is unmounted, but its retained action would store inline data URLs through an API that accepts arbitrary nonempty URLs without signature or scheme validation.
findings.impact: There is no active canonical /team exploit path, but a future legacy remount could reintroduce unsafe-scheme links and database/storage amplification without a fresh security review.
findings.likelyCause: Attachment metadata and file storage are conflated in one field.
findings.recommendation: Remove the dormant path, or gate any remount on private object storage, signed access, MIME/signature validation, scans, and quotas.
acceptanceCriteria: The orphaned action/component is removed or explicitly owned and tested before remount.
If retained, javascript:, file:, untrusted data:, and non-allowlisted remote URLs are rejected.
MIME extension and file signature mismatches are rejected.
Oversized and repeated uploads cannot amplify database storage.
Downloads require the same contact/appointment permission and are audited.

findings.subview: Password attempts, magic-link issue/exchange, and normalized identity
findings.dataState: repeated attempts, duplicate normalized identity, and concurrent exchange of one magic-link token
prerequisites: Repeated authentication requests
Ability to create duplicate normalized member identities
One valid magic-link token and two concurrent exchange callers
reproduction: Send repeated password attempts or magic-link requests; handlers contain no visible rate limiter, cooldown, lockout, or challenge.
Create two members from case/whitespace variants that normalize to the same stored email; the schema does not make that normalized value unique.
Request multiple magic links for one member; creation inserts each token without revoking prior unexpired tokens.
Issue two concurrent exchange-link requests for one valid token; both can SELECT it before either DELETE, and the unchecked delete does not gate either session insert.
findings.expected: Credential and delivery abuse is throttled per identity/IP/device, token replay is atomic, older links are invalidated according to a documented policy, and normalized login identity is unique.
findings.actual: No application-level throttling is visible; multiple rows can store the same normalized email; requesting links does not revoke older unexpired tokens; and token consumption is a non-transactional select/delete/session-insert whose delete result is unchecked.
findings.impact: Password guessing, SMS/email cost abuse, ambiguous account selection, and multiple sessions from concurrent reuse of one token are plausible or statically established.
findings.likelyCause: Anti-abuse was deferred to infrastructure and identity normalization is not expressed as a database invariant.
findings.recommendation: Add layered throttling/monitoring, a migration-safe normalized unique identity constraint, a documented prior-link invalidation policy, and atomic conditional token consumption before session insertion.
acceptanceCriteria: Documented thresholds return 429 without revealing account existence.
Expired and replayed tokens cannot create sessions, including concurrent exchange.
Duplicate normalized team identities are prevented or explicitly resolved.
Security events are privacy-safe and observable.

findings.surface: Team login, magic-link callback, and Settings
findings.subview: Stale-cookie recovery and first-login password setup handoff
findings.role: anonymous with invalid/expired cookie; newly authenticated team member
prerequisites: An invalid or expired myst-team-session cookie
Or a successful magic-link exchange returning needsPasswordSetup
reproduction: Place an expired or invalid myst-team-session cookie and open /team/login; cookie presence alone renders You're already signed in, while /team rejects the same token and redirects back to login.
Exchange a valid magic link whose response needs password setup; /team/auth redirects to /team?setup=1, but /team defaults to Inbox/Calendar and the setup prompt/form only exists in Settings.
findings.expected: Invalid cookies are validated/cleared before login rendering, and password setup lands on a visible, focused, announced Settings form.
findings.actual: Cookie presence can trap the user between login and /team, while the setup callback creates a valid session but lands on a default tab with no setup UI; users can recover only by manually navigating to Settings.
findings.impact: Users can be caught in a login loop or miss the intended optional first-login password prompt, increasing support load and leaving password sign-in undiscoverable until Settings is opened.
findings.likelyCause: Login UI trusts cookie presence instead of session validity, and the callback does not encode the tab that owns setup UI.
findings.recommendation: Validate and clear stale cookies on login; redirect setup to /team?tab=settings&setup=1 and manage focus/announcement.
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid/expired cookies never hide the login form and are cleared or safely replaced.
needsPasswordSetup redirects to /team?tab=settings&setup=1.
The password form is visible, receives deliberate focus, and its context is announced.
Back/refresh preserve a recoverable path without redirect loops.

prerequisites: Authenticated request with an invalid tab
reproduction: Load /team?tab=not-a-real-tab.
Observe activeTab falls back to the first nav item, but the tab variable remains invalid.
Observe every content branch checks the invalid value, leaving a shell with no tab content.
findings.expected: Unknown tabs canonically redirect to the role landing tab with a clear notice or render a deliberate not-found state.
findings.actual: The shell title/nav and content resolution can disagree, producing an empty main region.
findings.impact: Broken bookmarks or mistyped URLs look like missing data and are hard to recover from.
findings.likelyCause: Active navigation fallback is computed separately from content routing.
findings.recommendation: Normalize or redirect the route before nav/content rendering.
acceptanceCriteria: Every invalid tab produces one deterministic role-allowed destination.
The URL, selected navigation item, title, and content agree after refresh and Back/Forward.

findings.dataState: more than one page of threads
prerequisites: Thread count exceeds page size
reproduction: Use the Inbox pagination link, which writes inbox_offset.
Observe page.tsx hardcodes inboxOffset to undefined and passes no offset into InboxSection.
Observe the listing request remains on the first page.
findings.expected: Offset survives URL navigation, refresh, copy/paste, filters, and Back/Forward.
findings.actual: The pagination parameter is generated but discarded by the page resolver.
findings.impact: Older conversations become inaccessible through the primary Inbox list.
findings.likelyCause: Parameter rename/migration left parsing disabled.
findings.recommendation: Parse and validate inbox_offset consistently and add dense-data navigation tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Next/Previous changes the API offset and visible rows.
Pagination composes with all filters and survives refresh/history navigation.
Deleted/stale rows do not trap the user on an empty page.

prerequisites: At least two new leads including one outside the latest 12 contacts
reproduction: Dismiss one new lead for 24 hours.
Observe the action sets a global hidden-until cookie and hides the entire banner, not only that lead.
Observe discovery loads only 12 contacts before finding a new stage.
findings.expected: Dismissal is per lead/user, remaining leads stay discoverable, and queue counts derive from all eligible leads.
findings.actual: One dismissal hides all banners for 24 hours and discovery is limited to 12 contacts.
findings.impact: Staff may miss time-sensitive leads and speed-to-lead goals.
findings.likelyCause: A notification banner is standing in for a durable per-user queue state.
findings.recommendation: Back the queue with explicit lead/user acknowledgment state and accurate pagination/counts.
acceptanceCriteria: Dismissing lead A never hides lead B.
All eligible leads are reachable regardless of contact ordering.
State is consistent across sessions and audited when appropriate.

prerequisites: One upstream request fails
reproduction: Fail Partners list/directory requests and observe empty arrays with no primary error.
Fail Pipeline audit and observe the component returns null.
Fail Inbox provider health, failed sends, directory, detail, timeline, or AI ancillary calls and observe several are converted to empty/null.
findings.expected: The UI distinguishes true empty, partial data, stale cache, timeout, permission denied, and provider degradation.
findings.actual: Several failures disappear or become empty-looking states.
findings.impact: Staff cannot tell whether there is no work or the CRM failed to load it, risking missed tasks and unsafe retries.
findings.likelyCause: Broad catch-to-null patterns were used to keep composite pages rendering.
findings.recommendation: Track per-panel completeness and expose actionable partial-failure banners with retry and timestamp.
acceptanceCriteria: Every injected 401/403/404/409/422/429/500/malformed/timeout/offline state is distinguishable from empty.
Partial panels name stale or missing data and offer scoped retry.
No action is enabled using silently incomplete prerequisites.

prerequisites: Keyboard or screen reader
reproduction: Open the mobile navigation and press Escape; no key handler closes it.
Tab through the page; no focus trap/initial focus/return focus is implemented.
Collapse desktop navigation; collapse/expand and icon-only utility controls can lose visible/programmatic names.
Observe the mobile drawer reuses persisted desktop collapsed state.
findings.expected: A modal drawer traps and restores focus, closes with Escape, labels itself, and ignores desktop collapse state; every icon control has an accessible name.
findings.actual: The dialog has role/aria-modal but lacks modal keyboard behavior and shares collapse state.
findings.impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users can become disoriented or unable to close/navigate the shell.
findings.likelyCause: A visual drawer was implemented without a reusable dialog/focus primitive.
findings.recommendation: Use a tested dialog/navigation primitive and explicit accessible labels.
acceptanceCriteria: Focus enters the drawer, stays inside, Escape closes it, and focus returns to Open navigation.
Desktop collapse preference does not hide mobile drawer labels.
All interactive elements pass computed-name checks at every breakpoint.

findings.subview: Headings, loading, flash messages, and forms
findings.dataState: loading, success, error, and search forms
prerequisites: Keyboard/screen reader or reduced motion
reproduction: Inspect the modern shell title: it is a div and most tab surfaces start with h2, leaving no page h1.
Inspect TeamSkeletonCard: it animates without status/busy semantics or reduced-motion treatment.
Inspect flash messages: no live region is attached.
Inspect placeholder-only search inputs such as Contacts.
findings.expected: Each page has one descriptive h1; status changes are announced; loaders expose busy state and honor reduced motion; every input has a persistent label.
findings.actual: Heading hierarchy, live announcements, busy semantics, reduced-motion behavior, and labels are inconsistent or absent.
findings.impact: Screen-reader users receive weak page orientation and no reliable feedback after important actions.
findings.likelyCause: Accessibility semantics are applied component-by-component without a CRM form/status layer.
findings.recommendation: Establish shared page-header, field, status, dialog, table/card, and skeleton primitives and run WCAG 2.2 AA automation/manual journeys.
acceptanceCriteria: Every tab and modal has a correct heading/landmark hierarchy.
Success, warning, error, and loading changes are announced once without focus theft.
Critical journeys complete keyboard-only at 200% and 400% zoom.
Zero unexplained serious/critical automated violations remain.

findings.surface: Inbox, Pipeline, Contacts, and Owner HQ
findings.subview: Initial load, polling, dense data, and inactive views
prerequisites: Production-like seeded volume and trace tooling
reproduction: Inspect Inbox: five requests run in parallel, followed by serial contact timeline/summary/task/next-action work; live updates poll every 8 seconds and attachment media performs HEAD requests.
Inspect Pipeline: the entire board is requested with no page/window in the UI.
Inspect Contacts: directory/list/selected record are sequenced.
Inspect Owner HQ: revenue, expenses, commissions/payroll, and source data load before most view selection; Payments adds large reconciliation requests.
findings.expected: Only active-view critical data loads, polling cannot overlap, dense datasets are paginated/windowed, and user-specified Web Vitals targets are met over five runs.
findings.actual: Static request topology creates waterfall, polling, fan-out, and unbounded-data risk; no live trace could be captured because Chrome DevTools MCP and the app stack are unavailable.
findings.impact: Dense accounts and mobile connections may see slow navigation, background request contention, provider cost, and stale race conditions.
findings.likelyCause: Composite server components fetch independently without a per-tab data budget or cancellation/overlap policy.
findings.recommendation: Measure first with the specified profiles, then parallelize/cache/window by active view and replace per-item probes with batched metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: Five-run medians meet LCP <=2.5s, INP <=200ms, CLS <=0.1, and TTFB <=800ms for representative states.
Visible action feedback begins within 100ms.
Inbox polling has cancellation/single-flight behavior and no per-attachment HEAD fan-out.
Pipeline and reconciliation loads remain bounded at documented maximum volume.

prerequisites: NEXT_PUBLIC_GA4_ID or Google Ads tag configured
reproduction: Load a /team deep link while Google tags are configured.
Observe GoogleTag is mounted in the root layout that wraps /team.
Observe initial gtag config can send a page view for the current location; SPA page-view handling uses pathname only, creating inconsistent query treatment.
findings.expected: Authenticated CRM routes have an explicit privacy-safe telemetry policy; customer/resource IDs and message data never reach marketing vendors.
findings.actual: Marketing tags are globally mounted and no /team exclusion/redaction is visible at the root boundary.
findings.impact: Internal route metadata or identifiers may be sent to a marketing analytics provider, while useful privacy-safe CRM telemetry is absent.
findings.likelyCause: Public marketing and authenticated product surfaces share the root layout.
findings.recommendation: Exclude authenticated surfaces from marketing tags or enforce a documented allowlist/redaction boundary; add first-party privacy-safe product telemetry.
acceptanceCriteria: Network capture proves no contact/thread/message/report IDs or content reaches marketing providers from /team.
CRM telemetry uses stable non-PII event names and role-safe metadata.
Consent/privacy documentation matches actual authenticated-route behavior.

findings.subview: Automated regression and static quality gates
reproduction: List the configured Playwright suite: 115 cases exist, but desktop /team coverage is concentrated in one Inbox CRM workflow file.
Search for all-tab, role-matrix, axe, visual, and performance suites; none exist in the current default suite.
Run raw lint: 991 errors remain, including 126 errors and 6 warnings in /team; the ratchet passes because the baseline permits 1027.
findings.expected: All tabs, roles, critical journeys, accessibility, visual states, and high-risk mutations have deterministic gates; new lint debt is prevented and old debt is burned down.
findings.actual: The current gates can pass without broad /team coverage and with substantial grandfathered static debt.
findings.impact: Cross-tab and role regressions can ship undetected, especially where UI hiding substitutes for authorization.
findings.likelyCause: E2E investment grew around public/mobile flows and selected Inbox work rather than a canonical CRM risk matrix.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the separate audit suite, add provider fakes and DB assertions, then promote stable security/smoke/journey slices into CI.
acceptanceCriteria: All-tab smoke and forged-cookie/no-cookie proxy gates run on every PR.
Role matrix and seven critical journeys run in a deterministic nightly/staging suite.
Accessibility/visual/performance evidence covers the requested viewport/theme states.
The /team lint baseline trends to zero with no new violations.

prerequisites: Representative role usability sessions
reproduction: Compare Contacts and Pipeline detail; Sales HQ and Sales Log; Expenses/Commissions and Owner HQ; Policy and Automation; Agent and Simulated Chat; Ads, Analytics, and SEO.
Observe duplicate context and controls across top-level destinations, while advanced/high-risk panels are mixed with daily work.
findings.expected: Primary navigation reflects a small set of daily jobs; overlapping context and advanced administration are consolidated or progressively disclosed.
findings.actual: Twenty-three top-level tab IDs expose overlapping detail, reporting, agent, marketing, and administration mental models.
findings.impact: Discoverability and training cost rise; staff may use overlapping sources inconsistently.
findings.likelyCause: Capabilities were promoted to tabs as they shipped rather than through a durable task-based IA.
findings.recommendation: Retain five core anchors, consolidate Marketing, move Partners/Sales Log under Sales, and move agent/admin tools under explicit Advanced groups—pending staff validation.
acceptanceCriteria: Five role-representative sessions validate first-click accuracy, completion, time, errors, backtracks, assistance, and ease.
Every current tab has an agreed keep/simplify/combine/move/advanced/deprecate decision.
No critical task requires knowledge of two overlapping detail implementations.

findings.surface: Aliases, classic layout, documentation, and orphaned components
findings.subview: quote-builder, canvass, marketing, myday, estimates, legacy components
reproduction: Load each legacy tab alias and observe silent in-memory remapping.
Load quote-builder or canvass; page.tsx derives a quoteMode but QuotesHubSection does not destructure or use it, so canvass opens the generic Quotes workspace rather than CanvassSection.

From the modern shell, activate Classic layout; classicHref is built by a helper that returns the unchanged URL while the current page is modern, so the button pushes the same route without layout=classic.
Inspect unmounted CanvassSection, EstimatesSection, MyDaySection, and PaymentsSection.
Compare README/critical-flow coverage to the 23 canonical tab inventory; simulated-chat and many admin surfaces are omitted.
findings.expected: Supported routes, deprecation windows, canonical redirects, ownership, and documentation are explicit and measurable.
findings.actual: Aliases and a full classic shell increase the matrix; quote-builder/canvass submode intent is ignored; the modern Classic layout button is a no-op; and legacy components/docs obscure the current product boundary.
findings.impact: Regression cost and operator confusion persist; removal decisions cannot be evidence-based without usage telemetry.
findings.likelyCause: Incremental migrations retained compatibility paths without exit criteria.
findings.recommendation: Instrument privacy-safe alias/classic usage, set a deprecation threshold/date, redirect canonically, remove unreachable components, and update docs.
acceptanceCriteria: Every legacy alias has a canonical redirect and measured usage owner.
A retained canvass deep link reaches an intentionally supported canvass workflow, or redirects with a clear retirement notice; quoteMode is never silently ignored.
If retained, the modern Classic layout control changes to a URL containing layout=classic and direct desktop/phone compatibility smoke passes.
Classic is regression-only with documented parity boundaries and a retirement trigger.
Unreachable components are either mounted intentionally with tests or removed.
README and critical-flow docs match the canonical inventory.

findings.subview: Owner member update, deactivation, role change, and deletion
findings.dataState: self account or final active owner
prerequisites: One active owner, or an owner editing their own member record
reproduction: As the only active owner, PATCH the current member to active=false or assign a non-owner role.
Alternatively DELETE the same/last-owner member after the typed UI confirmation.
Observe that handlers authorize the current request but do not enforce a self-deactivation or last-active-owner invariant before the mutation.
findings.expected: At least one active recoverable owner always remains; self-deactivation/role loss/deletion requires a safe handoff and explicit session consequences.
findings.actual: The member PATCH/DELETE paths permit self or last-owner removal and rely on legacy break-glass recovery rather than a server invariant.
findings.impact: Administrators can lock all normal team-owner sessions out of Access and require break-glass recovery.
findings.likelyCause: Member CRUD validates fields and permissions but not organization-wide ownership invariants.
findings.recommendation: Enforce a transactional last-active-owner rule and require explicit ownership transfer/session-revocation messaging for self changes.
acceptanceCriteria: PATCH and DELETE return 409 without mutation when they would remove the last active owner.
Self-deactivation, self-role loss, and self-delete require an explicit supported handoff and immediately revoke affected sessions.
Concurrent owner removals cannot both pass the invariant.
The denied attempt and successful ownership transfer are attributed in Audit Log.

findings.dataState: more than 50 events or incident investigation
prerequisites: More than 50 events
reproduction: Open Audit Log with a production-like event history.
Observe the component requests/displays the latest 50 with no filter, search, pagination, correlation, export, or detail affordance.
Attempt to investigate a specific actor/entity/outcome outside the visible window.
findings.expected: Auditors can filter by actor, role, action, entity, outcome, and time; paginate through retained immutable data; inspect safe metadata and correlations.
findings.actual: The surface is a fixed recent feed that cannot support coverage verification or incident investigation.
findings.impact: Unauthorized or failed actions can be difficult to reconstruct, and the audit completeness matrix cannot be verified through the product.
findings.likelyCause: The tab began as an operational recent-events widget.
findings.recommendation: Define the audit event contract/retention first, then add server-side filtering, pagination, correlation, safe export, and tamper checks.
acceptanceCriteria: A sensitive-action coverage matrix passes for every tab.
Filters and cursor pagination find events beyond the first 50 deterministically.
Actor, role, entity, timestamp, outcome, and safe metadata are accurate for human and system actions.
Audit writes are transactionally consistent or independently durable without turning committed work into misleading failure.
